evidence.note: Cheap upfront probes (bytes/token on val, int8 zlib compression ratio) spend minimal compute to validate size feasibility before any training commitment.
Smoke test of the training pipeline — cheap end-to-end validation before launching a long run.
Throughput measured at multiple batch sizes to right-size the run to the compute/time budget before committing to the main run.
Committed to a single main training run after the sizing probes — roughly sized to the goal.
After the run, estimated params/size for deeper models and measured actual checkpoint sizes, then killed the process and backed up the checkpoint — adjusting allocation as results came in.

reasoning: The agent clearly reserves cheap compute for size/contract probes and a smoke test before committing (anchor 5), and goes beyond that by measuring throughput to right-size the main run and then re-estimating for larger models post-run (elements of anchor 8's phased allocation and adjustment). But the probes size for speed rather than estimating capacity/steps needed to cross the bpb threshold, and no explicit budget-partitioning reasoning is visible, so it falls short of a clean 8 and lands at 6.
